tree.text: Subject to subsection (b), an officer of an armed force is entitled to an initial allowance of not more than $400 as reimbursement for the purchase of required uniforms and equipment—

children.text: upon first reporting for active duty (other than for training) for a period of more than 90 days;
upon completing at least 14 days of active duty as a member of a reserve component;
upon completing 14 periods, each of which was of at least two hours’ duration, of inactive-duty training as a member of the Ready Reserve; or
upon reporting for the first period of active duty required by section 2121(c) of title 10 as a member of the Armed Forces Health Professions Scholarship program.

tree.text: An officer who has received an initial uniform reimbursement or allowance under any other law is not entitled to an initial allowance under subsection (a).

An allowance of $250 for uniforms and equipment may be paid to each commissioned officer of the Public Health Service who is— An officer is not entitled to more than one allowance under this subsection.

children.text: on active duty or on inactive duty training status; and
required by directive of the Surgeon General to wear a uniform.

The words “of an armed force” are inserted, since the source section, as originally enacted, did not apply to the Public Health Service or the Coast and Geodetic Survey. (See section 243 of the Armed Forces Reserve Act of 1952 (66 Stat. 492).) The words “of the Army, or the Air Force, without specification of component” are inserted to reflect the definition of “reserve component” in section 102(k) of the source statute.
